plan: SPEED_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN_2026-07.md 6.3 -> held-out v3 on stage-B demand
method: The frozen v2 held-out case set - same 12 cases, schedules, proxy and thresholds - rerun end to end on demand REBUILT under stage-B code. The cases were frozen before stage B existed, so they are genuinely held out with respect to it; only the demand generator changed. Isolated state root; live release guarded around every build and SUMO phase.
verdict: PASS on all five defined gate checks, each with margin.

caveats_stated_plainly.failure_recall_dropped: 0.867 -> 0.722, still above the 0.6 floor. B's demand disqualifies a slightly different borderline set than pre-B; the practical winner the proxy must preserve is preserved.
caveats_stated_plainly.spearman_sign_flip_is_noise_not_regressi: median_spearman went +0.894 -> -0.976, but it is computed on the ONE ranking case with any objective spread (v2-secondary-medium-weekend-4h), whose 8 eligible objectives span only 71s - entirely inside the 300s practical-equivalence band. Every eligible candidate there is a practical winner, so regret stays 0.0 and recall 1.0 despite the fine-order flip. The flip measures rank noise inside the band, not a decision-affecting ranking regression.
caveats_stated_plainly.case_set_weakness_reconfirmed: spearman_case_fraction is 1/7: six of seven ranking cases have near-tied objectives, so the v2 set cannot actually test ranking DISCRIMINATION at spreads beyond the equivalence band. A stronger v3 should include cases whose true objective spread exceeds 300s.

consequence: This is a legitimate held-out PASS of the gate as defined, on B demand - it satisfies the plan's 6.3 requirement to re-validate before global-best claims continue. But because it re-uses the weak v2 case set, it re-opens the claim at the SAME evidential strength v2 had, not a stronger one. Opening the global-best claim on B is therefore a defensible decision, not an automatic one; it is an outward-facing honesty-label choice for the owner.
